main_text.p: be,alter dives,alter pauper. Dives majo-rū minorumq; pecudum magnā copiam habebat. Pauper unam omnino habebat oviculā, à se emptam et enutrita, quæ u-nā cum ipso ejusq; filiis adoleverat, ejus cibo vescēs[?], ex ejus calice bibens, in ejus si-nu quiescēs: breviter erat ei pro filia. Ad illum diuitē venit hospes quidam, quem accepturus ille, parsit de suis minoribus majoribus ve sumere pecoribus:& captā illam pauperis oviculā, hospiti mactavit. Hic David in homine magna ira perci-tus, Nathani sic dicit: Per Iovam immore[?] tale, morte dignus est istius autor facino-ris, ovemq; quadruplo pensabit, qui istud cōmittere non dubitaverit. Et Nathan: Tu ille es, inquit. Ego te (inquit Iova De-us Israelitarū) regem in Israelitas unxi: ego te ab injuria Sauli defendi: tibi Do-mini tui domum, tibi domini tui uxores cōplectendas, tibi Israeliticam Iudaamq; stirpē dedi: alia atq; alia insuper datu-rus, si ea parum essent. Cur tu Iovam, con-temptis ejus præceptis, scelere tuo offendi sti? dum Uriam Hettæum ferro trucida-ti, ejusq; uxorem, eoper te Ammonitā-

page.notes: The first word is a fragment at the top edge of the scan ("be," with its first letter cut off) and stays a fragment. "vescēs" is uncertain: the letters are blurred. "immore[?] tale" is uncertain: the word may be "immortale" with a worn letter, and the line break shows no printed hyphen. "eoper" is read as printed. The last word ends in a hyphen and continues on the next page. No catchword or signature is visible.
